newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila places 20 pct tax on term reverse repos.
newsitem.headline: Manila places 20 pct tax on term reverse repos.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday it had been advised by the Bureau of Internal Revenue that it will start charging on January 2 a 20 percent final tax on the interest income of term reverse repos on January 2.
Reverse repos are instruments used by the Central Bank to control money supply.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said the 20 percent tax will be imposed on reverse repos with a term of six days or longer.
"Short-term monetary policy will not be affected," said Edeza, referring to the overnight borrowing of the Central Bank at the money market.

But for the longer term, "we may have to pay higher rates to entice people to place their money with us," he said. The Central Bank currently issues term reverse repos with maturities of one, two and three months.
The Central Bank had disagreed with the Bureau of Internal Revenue on the imposition of the tax on reverse repos because it had not been part of the list of instruments that should be taxed.
"They're now including it in the list of instruments that will be subject to the final tax," Edeza said.
The Bureau of Internal Revenue may have decided to include reverse repos because of the growing volume of transactions, Edeza said.
